# DSH ⇄ JetBrains

Small packages that connect a local DeepSeek Harness (DSH) to a JetBrains IDE, so the IDE and
the ag
ent share one workspace instead of two islands.
Each one works on its own: the IDE plugin and the DSH bundle are the two halves of the same workflow

, and
the session-link plugin only lets a page be asked for a session by address. The DSH bundle car

ries both a
Host half and a web-client half, so installing it covers the tool, the context line, and
Host half and a web-client half, so installing it covers the tool, the context line, and the clicks.
| Package | Platform | What it does |
| `jetbrains-companion/` | IntelliJ Platform plugin (Java, no Gradle) | **DSH Chat** tool window emb
edding DSH's own web client, one DSH session per IDE window, live workspace publication, a loopback
bridge so DSH can put a file in front of you, and a `DSH Changes` tool window that shows a published

turn as a native side-by-side IntelliJ diff. |
| `jetbrains-workspace/` | DSH profile bundle (host
half + web-client half, plain JavaScript) | Reads the IDE's workspace — including a module's multipl
e content roots from its `.iml` — into DSH as a tool, a runtime context line, and a registered works
pace. Works with the companion running or from the IDE's own state files after it closed. Sends open
ed and clicked files to the IDE: the Host half replaces DSH's default desktop opener, and the client

half redirects the Sidebar file viewer. |
| `jetbrains-session-link/` | DSH client plugin (plain Ja
vaScript) | Lets `#dsh-session=<id>` — or a hash change on an open page — select that session withou
t a reload. Optional: the chat panel falls back to the client's stored selection when it is absent.
a reload. Optional: the chat panel falls back to the client's stored selection when it is absent. |
> **Unofficial.** Neither package is made by, endorsed by, or affiliated with JetBrains or DeepSeek.

[该节后续省略]
## What you get
- **Chat inside the IDE.** The `DSH Chat` tool window renders DSH's web client, authenticated with t

he
same browser-session cookie DSH gives a browser, and opens the session for the window you are in.
- **One workspace, seen from both sides.** The window's root project and every attached module/VCS
directory reach the model as a runtime context line and as a `jetbrains_workspace` tool result, with

each directory labelled by the source that reported it.
- **Round trip.** DSH can read the active f

ile, caret and selection, and open a file in the IDE at a
line — with the companion's bridge, or wit
h the IDE state files when the IDE is closed.
- **Review a turn as a diff.** `DSH Changes` lists every turn `dsh-jetbrains-workspace` publishes an

d
opens any changed file as a native side-by-side IntelliJ diff. A turn's diff also opens by itself,

with a
**Keep** / **Revert** notification, the chat panel's toolbar has a **Changes** toggle, and r

everting works
per file or per hunk — refusing rather than half-reverting a file that changed since

the turn.
- **Nothing is lost while the IDE is closed.** The review document outlives the IDE: on th

e next start the
companion mentions the turns it missed, with one click to the panel.
## Why one DSH, not one per project
Because the value is in seeing everything at once. One Host process holds every session, so a reader

can keep
an agent running in one project under watch while working on something else in another ses

sion that has
nothing to do with the IDE. It is also why this bundle publishes one review document f

or the whole Host
rather than one per workspace: the changes panel lists the turns of every session

that changed files, so an
agent left running in another project still reports where the reader alrea

hanged files, so an
agent left running in another project still reports where the reader already is.
The IDE side leans the same way. One companion serves the whole IDE: the chat panel keeps one sessio

n per
project, the window junction can be told to register the shared parent so a multi-module check

out is one
workspace (`junctionRoot: common-parent`), and `jetbrains_workspace` answers for every at
ace (`junctionRoot: common-parent`), and `jetbrains_workspace` answers for every attached directory.
What that costs, measured rather than assumed: the companion descriptor is *one file per user*, and

the
companion starts **one bridge per IDE run**. Opening a second IDE window produced no second `bri

dge on` line,
and the one descriptor already named both windows' projects. So a Host reaches every w

indow through one
bridge, DSH's workspace tool sees all of them, and the companion decides which win

dow shows a diff or opens a
file by matching the path against each project's base path. The Host als

o accepts a *set* of descriptors (the
single one plus any `jetbrains-companion/*.json` beside it) an

d chooses by workspace, so a future build that
publishes one descriptor per window needs no Host cha

ooses by workspace, so a future build that
publishes one descriptor per window needs no Host change.
## What each half gives you
Each half is useful alone, and they do not depend on each other to install. What you get changes:
| Capability | IDE plugin only | DSH bundle only | Both |

| `DSH Chat` tool window in the IDE (embedded DSH client, cookie auth) | yes | — | yes |
| One DSH s
ession per IDE window, grouped in the DSH sidebar | yes — the panel registers the workspace and crea

tes or attaches the session itself | — | yes |
| The model knows which IDE window is open (runtime c

ontext line) | — | yes, from the IDE's state files, or live when the companion runs | yes |
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- A JetBrains IDE, build 243+ (`IC-243` or newer), with the bundled browser (JCEF).
- A JDK 21 toolc

hain for the IDE plugin build — the IDE's own JBR is enough.
- Node.js 20+ for the DSH bundle and it

s development checks.
- DSH from a version that exposes `workspace/create` returning `sessionIds` an

d `created`,
`workspace/rename`, `session/create` with either `cwd` or `workspaceId` + `sessionId`,

and
`workspace/archiveSession` — the API surface both halves are written against.
